summary: An agent's ```html-live title="..." block is a small HTML page (fragment or full document, at most 128 KB of UTF-8) that the desktop runs inside the message, in a <webview> with exactly the HTML preview pane's sandbox: the sb-html-preview partition, will-attach-webview hardening (no preload, no Node, sandbox, context isolation), denied popups, no navigation off the page, refused permissions and downloads, the dead proxy, the request filter that cancels everything except the page's own sb-preview://<token> origin, and the pane's CSP. It runs only once its fence has closed and it has scrolled into view; while it streams the card says Writing. The frame fits the page's reported height between 120 and 480 px, with Show all past 480. It shows loading, the error list with Send to agent and Show source, the N blocked list (with a hint naming the bundled copy of a blocked library), and too-large or unknown-library refusals that never run. At most two frames run per window (the newest in view, or one started with Run); the others pause as their still image. Source and Copy source sit in the header. Open in pane moves the page to the preview pane (the message keeps the image and In pane, one running copy); Save as file under More in the pane writes it into the chat's folder under a free name and the block becomes the normal HTML file card. Bundled libraries are served at /_sb/ (Chart.js 4.5.1, D3 7.9.0 and Three.js 0.170.0 vendored unmodified in resources/sb-live with their licences; Mermaid from the app's own dependency); nothing else loads. After a page is quiet for 1 s the desktop captures it and stores the still image on the chat's backend (a block that never comes into view is rendered hidden in a free running slot to take it), keyed by the SHA-256 of the block source (html_live_images_v1, admin scope to write). Phones never run agent scripts: they show that image (or No image yet), Source, Copy source and Open on desktop, which asks the backend to open the page in a desktop window's pane. Agents learn the block from one paragraph in the Switchboard MCP server's instructions.

notExercised: The Expo app and native Android were not run on a device or emulator: the image fit, the zoom view, the long-press sheet and the accessibility labels are verified only by tests and compilation.
iOS was not run (no simulator on this Mac).
Open on desktop against a remote headless backend: the event path is the same router subscription the desktop uses for other pushes, but it was exercised only against the local backend.

The jitter fix changes the desktop only: phones show the still image and never run the page, so they have no running-to-paused swap. A frame that never ran in this window still takes its first height when it first runs. An expanded frame that pauses keeps its expanded height. Its still image is taken again once the frame's height changes (Show all, or a new content height), so the image fills that box. Not driven in the built app: a frame that pauses less than 1 s after Show all still shows the folded image in the taller box.

Phones gain stills for blocks a desktop window mounted but never scrolled to (no phone code changed; they read the same html_live_images_v1 image). A block outside the chat list's mounted rows (beyond the virtualizer's overscan), or in a chat no desktop window opens, is still never rendered, so phones show No image yet for it. The hidden capture was exercised against the local backend only, not a remote one.
The translucent fix (2026-10-30) was not driven in the built app. A still image stored before it stays, keyed by the block source, so phones show the old image for that page.
